title: Dipeptidyl peptidase-IV inhibitor use associated with increased risk of ACE inhibitor-associated angioedema
authors: Brown NJ, Byiers S, Carr D, Maldonado M, Warner BA
population: Patients in phase III randomised trials of the DPP-4 inhibitor vildagliptin against comparator, with adjudicated angio-oedema events and concurrent ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker use from case report forms
funder: This work was funded by Novartis Pharmaceuticals and Novartis Pharma AG. Dr. Brown also received support from National Institutes of Health grant R01 HL079184.
authorConflicts: Byiers, Maldonado and Warner are employed by Novartis and Carr works at Novartis; Brown has received consulting fees from Novartis, consults for Merck, maker of sitagliptin, and holds a patent for identifying susceptibility to ACE-inhibitor angio-oedema.
result: Overall, vildagliptin was not associated with angio-oedema. Among patients taking an ACE inhibitor, confirmed angio-oedema occurred in 14 of 2754 vildagliptin users against 1 of 1819 comparator users (odds ratio 4.57, 95% CI 1.57 to 13.28). The authors propose reduced degradation of substance P, a DPP-4 substrate, and describe the absolute risk as small.
